newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco drafts tougher anti-drugs law.
newsitem.headline: Morocco drafts tougher anti-drugs law.

text.p: Morocco's interior ministry has drafted a law increasing the maximum jail term for drug traffickers to 30 years from 10 years, with a maximum fine of 800,000 dirhams ($85,000).
It said in a statement carried by the official news agency MAP on Monday that the move was in line with the United Nations recommendations on drug penalties.
The draft law includes a term of up to 15 years for promoting drug use, the statement said.

Interior Minister Driss Basri said recently that Morocco seized 103 tonnes of cannabis bound for Europe in 1996 and arrested more than 18,000 drug traffickers, including 342 foreigners. ($=9.39 dinars)
